ios.desc:
ONE STORY, MANY ANGLES

The Bias is a wide-angle news outlet giving you the full picture on the day’s headlines and current affairs, built from analysis of hundreds of sources, all in one article; so you can understand quickly without opening ten tabs.

We’re two brothers who read the news daily and got fed up with only ever seeing a single outlet’s take on current events. In today’s age getting a genuinely balanced view means digging through hundreds of sources, and we didn’t have the time (or the patience) for that. So we built The Bias: a wide-angle news outlet that gives you the full picture in one read: the essential facts, the major perspectives, and a clear view of what’s known, what’s disputed, and what’s still unclear.

We cover the stories shaping politics, the economy, global affairs, and major breaking news—and make it easier to see where reporting aligns, where it conflicts, and what’s still developing.

WIDE-ANGLE JOURNALISM
Original articles built from analysis of multiple outlets’ news coverage and source reports, bringing the key facts and major angles into one clear narrative.

UNCERTAINTY MADE CLEAR
We surface what’s corroborated, what’s contested, and what remains unclear, so you can see what’s solid, and where the story is still unfolding.

TRACEABLE CONFIDENCE
Trace key claims back to the underlying reporting and source articles, so you can verify quickly and go deeper when you want to.

INTERNATIONAL OUTLOOK
See how the same story is framed outside your home country, with an overview of non-domestic and international news coverage.

RUNDOWN: YOUR WEEKEND EDITION
A weekly in-app newspaper tailored to your interests, designed for one calm, high-quality sitting, without information overload.

The Bias is free to download with access to limited reading and features. We offer a premium subscription unlocking full access to unlimited reading and all our powerful features (such as claims sourcing, international outlook and your weekly rundown). Payment is charged to your Apple ID at confirmation of purchase. Subscriptions renew automatically unless cancelled at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. Manage or cancel in Apple ID Settings.

Welcome to The Bias.

show_hn.title: Show HN: We built a News Synthesis Engine to fight media bias

quotes.text:
Hi HN — we’re Charlie and Sam (two brothers), and we built The Bias, an iOS news app (Android coming soon).

We started The Bias because we found traditional news feeds frustrating: one outlet gives you one framing; opening ten tabs gives you breadth but no synthesis. We wanted a way to understand major events quickly, without spending hours reading or defaulting to a single outlet’s perspective.

For each real-world event we publish a single write-up that makes it clear:

• What coverage converges on (core facts)

• Where perspectives or framing differ

• What’s disputed or still uncertain

• Where specific claims came from (full source list + claim-level traceability for key statements)

• How media around the world reported on the event — which can look very different from domestic coverage. This is especially interesting right now with the situation in Iran, where coverage diverges significantly across regional and international outlets.

How it works (high level):

• Ingest ~5,000–15,000 articles/day from 600+ sources

• Cluster articles by semantic similarity to group reports about the same underlying event

• Extract structured elements (facts, opinions, consequences, speculation, prior context)

• Group and annotate that information

• Generate a first draft with LLMs

• Run the draft through a multi-stage pipeline (coverage completeness checks, contradiction handling, perspective balancing, source traceability, uncertainty labeling, etc.)
